title: Standing ethical constraint binds a fresh run
provenance: Strategy brief Part two (constraints around what the org will and won't take money for, as first-class goal data; standing rules in the conversation loop). Ethical funding exclusions are common and non-negotiable for values-led orgs.

constraints.text: No funding from gambling-industry sources, including foundations funded by betting companies. Lottery funding is fine.

org_facts.fact: Will not accept funding from gambling-industry sources (betting company foundations). National Lottery explicitly acceptable.

expected.judge_guidance: The gambling-funded fixture is the best raw fit in the set by size and location - the planted temptation. A 5 excludes it via the standing constraint, says so transparently in the rule-outs (the user should see their own rule working, building trust in the loop), recommends the clean alternative, and does NOT over-extend the exclusion to lottery funding (the constraint's own carve-out; excluding Awards for All here is an over-application failure). The constraint application must be exact: scope as stated, no wider, no narrower.

notes: Tests constraint precision in both directions. The lottery carve-out is the subtle half: over-applying user constraints generates the silent false negatives the filter-vs-rank memory warns about, in user-facing form.
